cursor.intention: Seek a genuinely functional way to reduce spoilage of known-safe food, rather than confuse physical testing or ground exposure with food-safety or preservation evidence.

args.name: Functional food preservation
args.function: Provide a learnable, physically grounded method to slow the actual spoilage of owned known-safe food. The existing paired ground-exposure trial explicitly cannot preserve food, so an observation-only substitute does not solve this problem.
args.conditions: Moss owns three roots and five berries with known zero toxicity. These foods are ageing. Moss is outdoors on ordinary soil, has no established tools, fuel supply or storage structure, and has not established hazelnut edibility. Any prerequisites must be explicit and obtained through actual work.
args.inputs: Potentially owned roots or berries plus whatever materials a supported method genuinely requires; suitable materials and quantities are currently unknown.
args.costs: Unknown. Specify real learning time, work, material requirements, ongoing costs, interruption handling and risks before use.
args.effects: If the world supports such a method, enable a measurable reduction in subsequent food decay through actual processing or storage. Do not grant replacement food, safety certification, equipment, mastery or preservation merely for requesting it. If no functional method is supported, state that limitation plainly.

Food keeps its existing decay. No reservation, drying, preservation, safety claim or reward is produced. A working operation needs a separately decided support representation and the installation of a reviewed moisture model; none is invented here.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 4000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form.
